# Phase 1 findings — the parallel-beam vertical slice

**Status:** COMPLETE 2026-08-04.  Gates measured on the Mac (CPU + MPS) and on
one H100 (gautschi job 14832690); all pass.
**Plan:** `port_plan.md` section 5 defines the Phase 1 scope and gates.
**Code:** the `mbirtorch` repo (staged); goldens are generated by
`tests/generate_goldens.py` in the mbirjax env and gitignored.

## Summary

The Phase 1 vertical slice is complete as a converging prototype, and every
gate passes with a large margin.  The projectors, the qGGMRF prior, the VCD
engine, FBP, auto-regularization, the Shepp-Logan phantom, and the
differentiable projector wrapper are ported; the full test suite (19 tests)
passes on CPU and MPS.  The strongest result is convergence parity: a seeded
mbirtorch recon reproduces a seeded mbirjax recon iteration for iteration at
the float-noise level (~1e-5), because the partition generators consume the
identical numpy RNG sequence and everything downstream is deterministic
arithmetic.  The measured cross-framework floors sit two orders of magnitude
inside the proposed golden tolerances, so those tolerances (1e-4 single-op,
1e-3 iterated) are confirmed with room to spare.

## What was ported

The package mirrors the mbirjax structure at Phase 1 scope: the portable fan
kernels and view-batched drivers, the parallel-beam geometry, the qGGMRF
gradient/Hessian with the single b_tilde source, numpy partitions, the VCD
engine with the on-device line search and positivity, the torch.fft row
filter, the auto-regularization chain, and the phantom generator.  Docstrings
and inline comments were copied from the mbirjax sources and adapted (Greg's
request, 2026-08-04).  Two mechanisms replaced jax machinery outright: buffer
donation became plain in-place ops, and the engine runs under
``torch.inference_mode``.  Deliberately deferred, per the plan: sharding, the
tile policy and Triton kernels, prox_map (Phase 2), checkpoint resume, and
YAML save/load.  Two additions beyond mbirjax serve the interop motivation:
``forward_project_differentiable`` / ``back_project_differentiable`` (custom
autograd Functions whose backward is the exact adjoint partner) and the
LEAP-style ``TorchProjector`` nn.Module.

## Gate results

**Adjointness.**  <Ax, y> = <x, A'y> holds within float noise on every
backend, and the differentiable wrapper's gradient equals the adjoint operator
at 1e-5 rel-max.

**Cross-framework goldens (CPU, vs jax 0.10.1).**  Measured rel-max floors,
against the 1e-4 single-op gate:

| quantity | rel-max vs mbirjax |
|---|---|
| sparse forward | 1.56e-06 |
| sparse back | 3.82e-07 |
| qGGMRF gradient / Hessian | 7.9e-08 / 6.0e-08 |
| Hessian diagonal | 1.22e-06 |
| FBP recon | 2.41e-06 |
| sigma_y / sigma_x / sigma_prox | exactly equal |
| Shepp-Logan phantom | exactly equal (0 of 262,144 voxels differ) |

The sigmas are exact because both sides run identical numpy statistics.  The
phantom is exact because the ellipsoid threshold happened to produce no
boundary flips at this size; the test allows a small flip fraction in general.

**Convergence parity (the iterated gate).**  A seeded 5-iteration recon on the
64-cell golden matches mbirjax: alpha trace 1.61e-05, fm_rmse trace 4.80e-06,
nmae trace 1.49e-05, final volume 1.17e-05 rel-max, against gates of 1e-2 /
1e-3 / 1e-3.  The mechanism is deliberate: ``gen_pixel_partition`` and the
subset shuffle are numpy-for-numpy ports with the same global np.random call
sequence, so both engines walk identical subsets in identical order.

**Backend smoke.**  The suite passes on CPU and MPS.  The demo (128^3
Shepp-Logan, 10 VCD iterations) runs on MPS in 4.3 s eager, final NRMSE 0.073
against the phantom.  These results indicate the Mac interactive experience is
already usable before any Phase 2 tuning.

## CUDA smoke (gautschi, one H100)

Job 14832690 (31 s wall, exit 0) ran the full suite plus the demo on one H100.
All 19 tests pass there too.  The golden floors on the node match the Mac's
(sparse forward 1.56e-06, back 3.06e-07, qGGMRF 7.9e-08, Hessian 1.14e-06,
FBP 2.22e-06; phantom exact), and the convergence-parity traces are even
tighter (alpha 3.17e-06, fm_rmse 3.83e-06, final recon 8.61e-06).  The demo on
CUDA reproduces the Mac's numbers exactly at the reported precision: 10
iterations, final forward loss 0.1717, NRMSE 0.0728, 4.36 s eager (the eager
H100 wall matching eager MPS is consistent with the Phase 0 finding that this
regime is not device-bound; Phase 2's compile pass is where the H100 pulls
ahead).

## Reading of the tolerances

The proposed golden tolerances survive contact with measurement.  Single-op
floors are ~1e-6 against a 1e-4 gate, and the iterated floor is ~1e-5 against
1e-3.  The gates stay as proposed; the floors above are the calibration record
for future drift comparisons.

## Remaining Phase 1 / handoff to Phase 2

Phase 1's remaining scope is small: prox_map (moved to Phase 2 by decision),
YAML save/load, and user-facing docs.  Phase 2 begins from a measured eager
baseline: the demo cell above, plus the Phase 0 spike numbers, are the
before-tuning reference points for the compile/batch-sweep work.
